html:
King Michael's coup was the arrest of the dictator Ion Antonescu by King Michael I of Romania in Bucharest on 23 August 1944, which took Romania out of its alliance with Nazi Germany and into the war on the Allied side.

The Soviet army had broken through in Moldavia days before. The young king, with opposition politicians and officers, called Antonescu to the palace, had him arrested, and announced the change on the radio. Romania turned its army on Germany, which opened the way for the Red Army into the Balkans and Hungary, and is often said to have shortened the war. But the Soviets occupied Romania anyway and put the communists in power. Michael was forced to abdicate in 1947. He returned after the revolution of 1989 and died in 2017. Antonescu was executed in 1946 after the end of the war.
sum: King Michael's coup was the arrest of the dictator Ion Antonescu by King Michael I of Romania in Bucharest on 23 August 1944, which took Romania out of its alliance with Nazi Germany and into the war on the Allied side.
